MVR GDTF matching and resolution

The initial MVR/App/Download source dialog remains the import entry point. Download rows subsequently use the existing GdtfDownloadQueueDialog presentation and its single native modal boundary. MvrGdtfResolutionDialog extends that presentation with a selected-row candidate list, available resource choices, full-catalog search and local-file selection. The importer delegates to RunMvrGdtfResolution and applies only final validated resource/mode pairs.

Ownership

  • mvr/gdtf_catalog_matcher.*: identity normalization and technical scoring.
  • mvr/gdtf_candidate_ranking.cpp: one catalog evaluation implementation, structured candidates and conservative automatic recommendation. The existing best-candidate adapter remains available to legacy consumers.
  • mvr/gdtf_patch_evidence.*: conservative repeated-address-spacing hints for manual review.
  • perastage_gdtf_matching: standard-library-only production target.
  • core/gdtf_resolution.*: typed source, proposed/applied choices, origin, fallback precedence, statuses and completion/cancellation transitions.
  • core/gdtf_resolution_resources.*: validation through the existing archive, description and mode readers; immutable copies into the import-owned scene workspace. The separate perastage_gdtf_resolution_resources adapter links existing readers. perastage_gdtf_resolution remains standard-library-only; the resource readers retain the existing wxBase ZIP dependency, not wxWidgets GUI controls.
  • gui/mvr_gdtf_resolution_workflow.*: catalog service, credentials, session retry, staging and composition of callbacks.
  • gui/mvr_gdtf_resolution_worker.cpp: bounded queue scheduling, background catalog analysis/download and event delivery; joins each worker before reuse.
  • gui/mvr_gdtf_resolution_actions.cpp: native picker, mode/review prompts and the existing GdtfSearchDialog in selection-only mode.

Ranking and confidence

Evaluate the parsed catalog once per fixture type, never during widget refresh. Keep eight useful revisions by default. Exact canonical identity precedes partial model evidence; safe candidates precede review candidates. Within a tier, retain stable technical ordering (authoritative identity, name, numeric compatibility, manufacturer, mode, footprint), then uploader metadata, modification time, rating and lexical revision ID. Reputation, recency and rating cannot promote a model variant to automatic eligibility. Roman numerals retain their established numeric normalization. Existing descriptive/version stripping remains a legacy search compatibility rule, not proof that two revisions are safe replacements.

Custom, Generic, Unknown, empty and No Manufacturer metadata are unknown. A catalog manufacturer's literal prefix may be removed from the imported model for canonical comparison; substring matches do not establish manufacturer identity. When exactly one manufacturer prefix is supported by exact model evidence, conflicting catalog manufacturer metadata requires review. Multiple supported manufacturer prefixes remain ambiguous. Known conflicting manufacturers require review. Catalog UUID and FixtureTypeID are logged separately; neither establishes revision identity or model equivalence.

Automatic recommendation requires exact canonical model identity, no manufacturer or numeric conflict, an identified compatible mode and agreement with any known footprint. Mode-digit or footprint-only evidence remains available for review. A matching footprint never proves channel semantics. Tied competing model identities or manufacturers without supporting prefix evidence are ambiguous. Confidence is Safe, Review, Ambiguous or NoMatch; only Safe can supply a recommendation. Full-catalog manual selection can intentionally choose another model, after a compatibility prompt and explicit mode selection.

The legacy SelectBestDownloadMatch retains its established fuzzy best-candidate contract for existing consumers. It is not the automatic-apply policy. New import code consumes RankDownloadCandidates through gdtf_resolution::Analyze.

Selection and application lifecycle

Resolution.selected is the proposal; Resolution.applied is the validated resource to commit. Explicit user selection takes precedence over automatic recommendation. Choosing an existing MVR, application or local profile also records it as the fallback for later catalog attempts. A failed revision retains that valid fallback and the proposed revision for inspection/retry. The low-level Cancel transition preserves applied choices for other consumers. The interactive MVR queue instead treats cancellation as rollback: every row returns its original MVR path with an empty mode override, preserving each instance's imported mode. The workflow also checks the modal return code before applying results. Late completion cannot replace a different proposal. Reuse is keyed by exact revision and mode and checks that the retained file and mode still exist.

Only structurally usable resources/modes appear in the existing-source selector. No fallback mode is guessed from matching footprint or address spacing. Local files and downloaded packages are read with shared Core services and copied to unique names under resolved-gdtf/ in the import workspace. The scene's existing resource lease owns their lifetime; original files, the MVR archive and the application library are not overwritten. A downloaded automatic replacement is validated against actual package identity, manufacturer, mode and footprint before commit. Missing catalog mode metadata is resolved from the downloaded package for explicit user selections.

After processing, the user can select any row, including successful rows, revise its proposal, and apply again. Acknowledgement is disabled while proposals are pending or work is active. The existing MVR preference mvr_auto_close_gdtf_download_window retains its default off and its existing Preferences → MVR Import/Export location; the queue has no preference checkbox. Enabled automatic close commits safe final choices without a confirmation prompt. Ambiguity, unresolved resources or failures keep the queue open for review.

Download, reuse and local selection use green success styling; original MVR and application fallback use amber; failures and unresolved profiles use red; canceled rows use muted styling. Candidate labels list every known mode/footprint and explicitly mark absent metadata as unavailable. Actual downloaded modes enrich the row. Original package mode counts supplement imported evidence. Repeated same-universe patch spacing (at least two equal adjacent intervals for one type and mode, no duplicate/invalid addresses) can preselect a mode for manual review; it never changes authoritative footprint evidence or automatic eligibility.

The modal queue appears before credential-store reads. Catalog, saved-credential login and downloads run in its worker. Only native credential entry and warnings run on the GUI thread. A 250 ms activity timer shows elapsed phase time; row events publish analysis results and progress incrementally. Original/application profiles are parsed once per unique path; canonical request models are reused per manufacturer during ranking. Ranking checks cancellation between catalog entries. Technical logs record catalog load, per-row profile-read and ranking times separately. Login, catalog and download use libcurl's multi interface with 100 ms polling for cancellation, including connection setup, while retaining established timeouts. Synchronous secure-store calls and individual archive/JSON reads are not interruptible; cancellation checkpoints surround those operations.

Cancel, Escape and window close request rollback both during work and after completion. The worker unwinds and joins before the single modal boundary returns; late results cannot commit a substitution after cancellation. Only OK or successful automatic close accepts the queue choices. Other explicitly chosen sources in the preceding MVR/App/Download dialog retain their independent choices.

Application updates every instance with the originating fixture-type key. Explicit queue modes bypass the importer's permissive mode resolver after validation. Fixture UUIDs, labels/type keys, addresses, transforms, groups and unrelated types are not rewritten. Existing project resource consolidation/export owns MVR publication; no extension XML or alternate package format is introduced.

Future command and protocol boundary

The existing CLI reads files through Inspection Core and dispatches typed semantic operations through Command Core and local IPC. OSC is a frontend adapter; the MCP adapter delegates to the CLI. None needs a dialog to call these new domain APIs.

A future adapter can expose analysis inputs (identity evidence, immutable catalog snapshot, existing validated resources and optional explicit Choice) and serialize CandidateRanking/Resolution to JSON. A separate mutation command would acquire an import/project resource lease, resolve a revision and mode, validate bytes, and atomically apply the final resource map through the normal project transaction. Inspection Core remains read-only; catalog acquisition/download is outside it.

No new CLI command, OSC route or MCP tool is registered. Blockers are a versioned JSON schema for evidence/reasons/statuses, a headless credential/cancellation policy, an import-session/resource handle, and a Command Core transaction adapter for applying replacements to an active scene. The standard-only matching target can already be linked independently; package validation uses the existing Core read target and wxBase ZIP runtime.

Validation

MvrGdtfImportMatching retains the existing regressions. GdtfResolution covers ranked revisions, generic/prefixed manufacturers, Roman numerals, ambiguity, model/mode/footprint mismatches, UUID non-equivalence and manual/fallback/reuse/ cancellation precedence. GdtfResolutionResources covers local package identity, modes, immutable ownership, malformed/missing definitions and failed publication. MvrGdtfResolutionDialog exercises automatic completion, successful-row changes, independent aliases, exact revision reuse, cancellation and offline fallback with an injected deterministic backend. Existing catalog and queue lifecycle tests remain in place. GdtfResolutionBoundary guards the new separation.

The Tivoli binary was not available. Tests use explicitly synthetic metadata and small generated packages and do not contact GDTF Share.

Types with several imported DMX modes require review before a catalog replacement. Validated MVR/application fallbacks can preserve the full imported mode set; a mode explicitly chosen by the user applies to every instance of that type. This prevents an automatic suggestion based on the first instance from silently rewriting other instances' modes. Address spacing is not treated as a verified GDTF footprint.

Apply selections retries failed catalog rows. An authentication cancellation or failure stops pending attempts as one batch, retaining every valid fallback and completed result without repeating the sign-in dialog for each row.
